subject: Next steps: PrivateNet deployment — egress ownership & allowlist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tim Bryant <tim.bryant@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Private VPC next steps & questions

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into security review. High-level summary: Ledgerly prefers an isolated deployment for production data, and the team is evaluating Private VPC (PrivateLink or VPC peering) vs Dedicated GPU pools. From our side, Private VPC gives you the most isolation; Dedicated can be an alternative if you want Redwood-managed egress and simpler networking.

Action items we captured: 
- Ledgerly: confirm whether you want Redwood-managed egress IPs (we provide static egress addresses) or customer-managed egress (your NAT/GW) — Tim to confirm by EOD Thu.
- Redwood (Karthik): provide decision matrix (Privatelink vs Peering) and a provisional list of egress IPs we use for Private deployments so your firewall team can start an initial allowlist.
- Redwood (Aditya): share the minimal deployment-checklist and the architecture diagram we discussed.

I attached a lightweight deployment-checklist to use in your security review. Suggested timeline: security review this week, procurement the following week, and tentative deployment window in early Dec if everything is green.

If you want, we can run a 30-min technical sync with your network/security engineer to walk through DNS, routing, and the allowlist. Proposed slots: Fri 11/12 10–10:30am PT or Mon 11/15 9–9:30am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: deployment-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Tim Bryant <tim.bryant@ledgerly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2027-11-11T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private VPC next steps & questions

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) On egress ownership: our security team prefers customer-managed egress where possible (we route outbound through our NAT and can apply existing inspection rules). That said, if Redwood can guarantee static egress IPs and an SLA for the PrivateLink path, we can consider Redwood-managed egress for a faster rollout.

2) For allowlisting we need: final egress IP list (or per-region ranges), FQDNs used by PrivateLink endpoints (if applicable), and estimated timing for when those endpoints will be provisioned so we can add temporary rules.

Sarah (cc) is our lead network engineer — she will drive the firewall/allowlist work. Can you include an expected expiry window for any temporary IPs you provide so we know when to remove them?

I'll try to make the Mon 11/15 9am PT slot work for Sarah. Also attaching a short firewall policy excerpt to speed the review.

—
Tim Bryant
Head of Infrastructure | Ledgerly
tim.bryant@ledgerly.com
Attachment: ledgerly-firewall-policy-stub.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Tim Bryant <tim.bryant@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-12T11:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private VPC next steps & questions

Hi Tim / Sarah — quick technical note to make the decision easier. Two production-ready patterns we recommend for Ledgerly based on today’s constraints: 

A) PrivateLink (recommended for SaaS-like integrations): 
- Redwood provisions PrivateLink endpoints in your account (or we provide service endpoints depending on cloud).
- Traffic terminates at the PrivateLink interface; outbound egress can be either customer-managed (recommended if you have inspection requirements) or Redwood-managed.
- Minimal routing changes on your side; DNS is the primary config (we provide endpoint DNS names).
- Egress IPs (Redwood-managed): we can provision a small pool of static IPs per region. Provisional sample IPs for planning only: 34.198.210.45, 34.198.210.46, 34.198.210.47. We will provide definitive ranges before provisioning.

B) VPC Peering (recommended if you want full L3 visibility): 
- Full routing between networks; your NAT handles outbound egress, so Redwood traffic will egress under your IPs (customer-managed egress).
- Requires route table updates and potential BGP consideration for complex topologies.

Recommendation for Ledgerly: If you want to keep existing inspection/NDR tooling inline, choose VPC peering so egress remains under your control. If you prefer faster ops and less routing work, PrivateLink with customer-managed egress is a good middle ground — we can also offer Redwood-managed egress if you accept our static IPs and the slight tradeoff on inspection.

Next technical deliverables we will share by EOD Fri: 
- Decision matrix (Privatelink vs Peering)
- A short runbook for allowlist entries (DNS, IPs, port list)
- Architecture diagram (attachment coming from Aditya)

Let us know if you want Redwood to provision temporary IPs for pre-prod testing; those will have an expiry we control (we’ll include dates in the list).

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: (provisional egress IPs listed inline)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: PrivateNet recommendation + attachments (architecture & MAP)

Tim / Sarah — following up with the consolidated recommendation and next steps.

Attached: redwood-privatelink-architecture-diagram.pdf and mutual-action-plan.docx (MAP). The MAP includes milestones, owners, and a suggested cutover window. Quick highlights: 
- Recommended path: PrivateLink with customer-managed egress. This keeps your inspection/NDR intact while minimizing route changes.
- If you decide on Redwood-managed egress instead, we will provide a signed appendix in the contract that lists the static IPs and our change notification process.

Immediate asks for Ledgerly security team: 
1) Confirm whether you prefer customer-managed or Redwood-managed egress (reply: "customer" or "redwood" by 2027-11-16 end of day).
2) If customer-managed: share the IP ranges you expect to use for NAT so we can validate routes.
3) Suggest a time for a 30-minute config walkthrough (we proposed Mon 11/15 earlier — if that’s tight, Wed 11/17 10am PT also works).

We’ve also included the minimal port list in the MAP (HTTPS, mTLS for control-plane notifications).

Next internal steps (owner in parentheses): 
- Karthik: finalize decision matrix and runbook (EOD Fri).
- Aditya: generate the provisional PrivateLink endpoint FQDNs and the temporary IPs for pre-prod (if requested).
- Marissa: coordinate kickoff and finalize MAP with Ledgerly.

Thanks — I’ll hold a calendar placeholder for Wed 11/17 10am PT until I hear back.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-privatelink-architecture-diagram.pdf, mutual-action-plan.docx

Subject: Re: PrivateNet recommendation + attachments (architecture & MAP)

Thanks Marissa / Karthik — we reviewed internally. 

Decision: customer-managed egress. We prefer VPC peering if Redwood can support route exchange patterns for our multi-account setup, but we are open to PrivateLink with customer-managed egress if peering introduces too much cross-account complexity. We need a short tech sync with our network lead (Sarah) to confirm.

Sarah’s contact details: sarah.jones@ledgerly.com, +1 415-555-0179. She’ll be on the call to confirm NAT IPs and our route requirements. We’ve attached a slightly expanded firewall policy excerpt for your network team.

Next steps from Ledgerly: Sarah will confirm our NAT egress IP ranges on the sync and provide any ACL templates they require. Can Redwood provide the Peering prerequisites checklist (CIDR constraints, expected route table changes) and a PrivateLink FQDN example by EOD Tues so Sarah can start an internal ticket?

We can do Wed 11/17 10am PT — Sarah confirmed. Please send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—
